## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Samasīsakathā* ("Discussion of Same-headedness") is the seventh treatise of the third section of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga*, comprising one of the thirty analytical treatises that systematize key doctrinal topics of the Pali Canon [Hazra 1994; SuttaCentral]. The text focuses on the concept of the *samasīsa* (literally "equal-headed one"), designating an individual in whom the attainment of arahantship—the exhaustion of defilements or craving—and the exhaustion of physical life occur at the exact same moment, leaving no intervening duration between enlightenment and final nirvana [Collins, Nirvana; Hazra 1994]. SuttaCentral lists four modern translations across four languages [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral identify an internal passage-level parallel between the *Samasīsakathā* and the opening *Ñāṇakathā* (Ps 1.1) of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* [SuttaCentral]. Automatically computed text-reuse data from DharmaNexus strongly confirms this link, identifying 39 matching passages totaling over 4,600 characters between the two texts, particularly between §0.3–6.2_3 and §472.1–476.2_3 with a 0.94 similarity score [DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus records substantial text sharing across other sections of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga*, including the *Balakathā* (Ps 2.9), *Suññakathā* (Ps 2.10), and *Mātikākathā* (Ps 3.10), as well as doctrinal matrices in the Abhidhamma *Dhammasaṅgaṇī* (*Dukanikkhepa*, Ds 2.3.2) and commentary texts such as the *Udāna-aṭṭhakathā* and *Mūlapaṇṇāsa-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language alignment, DharmaNexus notes low-level shared passages with the Tibetan translation of the *Saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtaviniścaya* (D3897) [DharmaNexus].
